text.p: These are the leading stories in Pakistani newspapers on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Para-military Rangers have set up pickets and checkposts in a number of areas in Karachi to avert any incident of sectarian violence during the Islamic lunar calendar month of Muharram.
- Five people were killed in Punjab province in incidents of sectarian violence on Friday night and Saturday.
- The Accountability Ordinance is being amended to provide for trial by single judges of high courts, Attorney General Chaudhry Mohammad Farooq said.
- According to latest figures given by officials, at least 115 Pakistanis and 94 Indians were killed in the huge fire that swept through Moslem pilgrim camps last month at Mina, Saudi Arabia.
- The Export Promotion Bureau is expected to be converted into a statutory body fully autonomous to take bold decisions for increasing Pakistan's exports.
- Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves slipped to $883.91 million on April 26 from $909.89 million a week ago, showing a decline of $25.89 million.
THE NEWS
- The government has decided to deploy army in sensitive areas of the country to maintain peace during the Moslem mourning period of Muharram.

- Six officials of the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) were arrested on Saturday on charges of corruption on the orders of the Ehtsab (accountability) Cell of the Prime Minister's Sectariat. Cases have been registered against a total of 11 CAA officials for allegedly committing financial fraud in the extension and refurbishing of the Islamabad airport terminal.
- A four-member delegation of the Awami National Party met President Farooq Leghari in Islamabad on Saturday and apprised him of their party's opposition to the controversial Kalabagh dam project.
- The Pakistani government has decided to promote relations with Russia, and foreign ministries of the two countries have agreed to sign nine accords on ministerial level this year.
- The Pakistan People's Party has set up as Ehtsab (accountability) cell to counter what it terms as one-sided accountability in the country.
THE MUSLIM

- For the first time in Pakistan's parliamentary history, the government has allowed Pakistan Television to telecast procedings of question hours of the National Assembly (lower house) and the Senate (upper house) from May 5. Initially the proceedings will not be shown live because of paucity of funds, but eventually they will be shown live from the parliament house, according to official sources.
- The administration in Gilgit, in nothern Pakistan, has arrested 12 Moslems from China's Xinjiang province who had illegaly crossed into the area from the Shamshal Pass a few days ago.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- South Korea is interested in importing onyx powder from Pakistan in a huge quantity, Park Kyung, the leader of a 10-member trade mission from Korea's Chungnom province said.

- About 15 billion cubic feet of natural gas reservoirs have been found along Balochistan province coast, particularly in Gwadar and Pasni coastal areas, by an American oil and gas company, United Meridian Corporation.
--Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
